purpose: Item 2 of the laptop strengthening (16 Nov 2026): published split-computing results re-read against paper 1's break-even rule. Every value is quoted from the paper at the location given (arXiv versions read 16 Nov 2026); nothing is estimated.

papers.cite: Banitalebi-Dehkordi et al., Auto-Split, KDD 2021, arXiv 2108.13041
papers.headline_image_baseline: uncompressed image (Table 8: Cloud-Only normalized latency 1, mAP 0.39)
papers.headline_claim: Table 8, 1 Mbps: Auto-Split normalized latency 0.26 vs 1 (mAP 0.37 vs 0.39); 3 Mbps 0.37 vs 1
papers.own_ablation: Table 7 (Appendix): Cloud-Only JPEG q60 mAP 0.35, normalized latency 0.15; q80 mAP 0.38, 0.23; Auto-Split lossless mAP 0.35, 0.08; JPEG on a Raspberry Pi 3 costs 28 ms (Cloud-Only) and 9 ms (Auto-Split features)
papers.rule_reading: Against the accuracy-matched JPEG of its own ablation (q60, mAP 0.35) the split's latency advantage falls from 12.5x (0.08 vs 1.0, raw image) to 1.9x (0.08 vs 0.15)

table.reading: 12.5$\times$ faster than raw; 1.9$\times$ against its own JPEG Q60 at equal mAP

papers.cite: Matsubara and Levorato, Neural compression and filtering for edge-assisted real-time object detection in challenged networks, ICPR 2020, arXiv 2007.15818
papers.headline_image_baseline: JPEG of the resized COCO image at its stored quality (Sec. VI), with the unmodified teacher (Faster R-CNN 0.370 bbox mAP, Table III)
papers.headline_claim: Sec. VI, Fig. 5b: gain over pure offloading up to 1.5 for poor channels; threshold 1 hit at about 8 Mbps
papers.own_numbers: Table IV: 8-bit bottleneck is 0.643 x the JPEG size; Table III: Faster R-CNN with 8-bit bottleneck 0.355 bbox mAP vs 0.370 teacher
papers.rule_reading: The code (0.355 mAP) is compared with a JPEG that keeps the teacher's 0.370; an accuracy-matched JPEG would be smaller, which lowers the 8 Mbps crossover (paper 1, Corollary: B_be depends only on the matching image setting's size)

table.baseline: JPEG at stored quality, unsplit detector
table.reading: code at 0.355 mAP against an image at 0.370: not accuracy-matched

papers.cite: Matsubara and Levorato, Split computing for complex object detectors: challenges and preliminary results, EMDL 2020, arXiv 2007.13312
papers.headline_image_baseline: the raw input tensor (Sec. 4: bottlenecks save 80.3-93.4 % of tensor size compared to edge computing)
papers.rule_reading: No compressed image baseline: the saving is against the uncompressed input tensor

papers.cite: Matsubara et al., BottleFit, WoWMoM 2022, arXiv 2201.02693
papers.headline_image_baseline: the average JPEG file of ImageNet, resized and center-cropped to 224x224 (Sec. on SP1), one quality
papers.headline_claim: Fig. 9: BottleFit offers lower delay than edge offloading when the Wi-Fi link quality decreases; the quantized bottleneck saves up to 93 % (SP1) / 98 % (SP2) of the JPEG input size
papers.rule_reading: Fixed JPEG quality: the image is not lowered to the bottleneck's (lower) accuracy

table.reading: image not lowered to the code's accuracy

papers.cite: Zhong and Chen, High-Efficiency Split Computing for Cooperative Edge Systems (HECS-B), arXiv 2504.15295
papers.headline_image_baseline: WebP and PNG (Table 2), one setting each
papers.headline_claim: Table 2, Nano, 4G 12 Mbps: HECS-B total 20.20 ms (transfer 10.90) vs WebP 62.63 ms (transfer 40.48)
papers.own_numbers: Table 2: non-transfer time 9.30 ms for HECS-B vs 22.15 ms for WebP on the Nano at every data rate
papers.rule_reading: Its split path takes less non-transfer time than the image path (9.30 vs 22.15 ms), so the rule gives no finite break-even: the code wins at every goodput, as the table shows. A fast-device case, consistent with the rule

table.reading: split path faster than the image path: no finite $B_{\mathrm{be}}$, wins everywhere
